BYD (BYDDY) Q3 profit jumps 28% on exports, but inventory balloons 60%

ER
By Elena Rostova Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst • via Electrek Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Electrek Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months.
  • But the rest of the filing is messier.
  • BYD’s inventory is up 60% since January, its cash pile has shrunk by almost half, and profit is still down for the first nine months of the year.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • ELENA ROSTOVA Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst

Capital Allocation Across Global Automakers

From an institutional perspective, the economic figures outlined in this dispatch from Electrek reflect monumental shifts in automotive capital. Legacy original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and agile EV startups alike must balance heavy gigafactory capital expenditures against fluctuating consumer demand and trade tariffs. Supply chain resilience—especially across lithium, cathode precursor materials, and semiconductors—is determining profitability.

Big Picture: Upcoming quarterly delivery reports and operating margins will indicate which manufacturers are successfully navigating the EV transformation curve.

BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months.

📌 The Core Development

But the rest of the filing is messier. BYD’s inventory is up 60% since January, its cash pile has shrunk by almost half, and profit is still down for the first nine months of the year.

BYD is still operating at a high level, but its business is changing.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

BYD filed its third-quarter report with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday. Here are the key figures for July through September:

That’s BYD’s best quarterly profit since the end of 2024, and the first time revenue has grown year-over-year after four straight quarters of declines.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

It’s also a big rebound from the start of the year. BYD’s Q1 2026 profit collapsed 55% to ¥4.08 billion, before recovering to ¥8.24 billion in Q2.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Still, it came in under expectations. Brokerages polled by Reuters were looking for ¥11.4 billion to ¥12.95 billion.

And zoom out to the full year so far, and BYD is treading water. Revenue for the first nine months was ¥566.30 billion, up just 0.01%, while net profit fell 4.2% to ¥22.34 billion. That’s on top of 2025, when BYD’s annual profit had already dropped to ¥32.62 billion from ¥40.25 billion in 2024.
